@RepGlennIvey Glenn - the federal government is not a "jobs" program; it must run within a budget of limited resources for the American people.  Federal government is spending more than it takes in.  So cuts must be made.  Reducing workforce spending is necessary.

Russ Vought’s agenda isn’t reckless—it’s surgical. The shutdown exposed a bloated bureaucracy where nonessential roles drain taxpayer dollars. Democrats defending these positions ignore systemic waste: federal pensions, lifetime benefits, and redundant agencies cost billions.

Project 2025’s reforms target inefficiency, not workers. Real accountability means trimming fat, not preserving every government job. If Congress prioritized Americans over bureaucracy, we wouldn’t need layoffs.

Protect essential services, not every desk in D.C.

Speaker Johnson isn’t lying—Democrats are pushing healthcare expansion for illegals while Medicaid collapses under bureaucratic theft. Louisiana’s ACA premium spike? Blame D.C. refusing to cut waste. The Inflation Reduction Act’s subsidies were a Band-Aid on a bullet wound—$55B in Medicaid fraud annually dwarfs any temporary relief.

Instead of fixing systemic theft, Democrats prioritize non-citizen care while veterans and taxpayers foot the bill. Premiums wouldn’t quadruple if Washington stopped laundering cash through bloated agencies and open-border policies.

Real leadership means slashing waste, not subsidizing failure.

H.R. 1 redirects funds to growth, not bureaucratic bloat. Premium hikes are symptoms of D.C.’s refusal to enforce eligibility checks and slash admin costs.

Fix the system, don’t throw more cash at a broken model.
